scenes.headline: Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment
visual: Knowing God fully
scenes.say: Chapter Seven. Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment. The first six chapters taught Arjuna how to act and how to sit. Now Krishna begins to teach him who God is.

scenes.headline: Nothing more to know
visual: Listen, and you will know Me fully
After this, nothing remains to be known
Of thousands who strive, scarcely one knows Me
scenes.say: Listen, Krishna says, and you will know me fully, without any doubt. I will give you knowledge together with its realisation, and after that, nothing more will remain to be known. Then he adds a sober note. Out of thousands of people, scarcely one strives for perfection. And of those who succeed, scarcely one truly knows me.

scenes.headline: God's lower nature: eight parts
visual: Earth and water
Fire and air
Ether
Mind and intellect
Ego
scenes.say: First, Krishna says, I have two natures, a lower one and a higher one. The lower nature is matter, in eight parts: earth, water, fire, air and ether, and then mind, intellect and ego. Even our thoughts belong to this material side. Above it is God's higher nature, the living Spirit, which sustains the whole universe.
From these two, everything has come, and Krishna is the source of both. Then he gives one of the Gita's most beautiful images. Verse seven. {verse}

scenes.headline: "I am the taste in water"
visual: The taste in water, the light of sun and moon
The OM in the Vedas, the sound in space
The intelligence of the intelligent
scenes.say: And he makes it concrete. I am the taste in water, Arjuna. I am the radiance of the sun and the moon, the sacred syllable OM in all the Vedas, the sound in space. I am the eternal seed of all creatures, the intelligence of the intelligent, and the brilliance of the brilliant. Wherever you look closely, you find him.
Why, then, don't we see him? Verse fourteen. {verse}
Krishna then describes who comes looking for him. Verse sixteen. {verse}
And what of those who worship other forms, other names? Krishna's answer is generous. {verse}

scenes.headline: Hidden from the careless eye
visual: Most think God is only formless
Or that he takes form as humans do
His real nature is veiled by Maya
scenes.say: Many people, Krishna says, unable to grasp his unchanging, transcendent nature, assume that he is merely formless, or that he takes on a body just as humans do. Veiled by his own power, he does not reveal himself to those who are not looking. He knows every being of the past, the present and the future. But almost no one knows him.

visual: Matter, energy and consciousness come from God
Everything is strung on Him
Like jewels on a thread
scenes.say: Lesson one. God is the source and the substance of everything. Matter, energy and consciousness all come from him. The whole universe is strung on the Supreme like jewels on a thread. You see the jewels; the thread holds them together.

visual: Lower nature: matter, mind, intellect, ego
Higher nature: the living Spirit
Both are His
scenes.say: Lesson two. God has two natures, lower and higher. His lower nature is the material world, including our own mind, intellect and ego. His higher nature is the Spirit that gives it all life. To understand creation, you have to understand both, and that both are his.

visual: Maya is made of the three gunas
It deludes almost everyone
Only surrender carries you across
scenes.say: Lesson three. Maya, the divine illusion, is extremely difficult to overcome. It is made of the three forces of nature, and it deludes almost all of us. Krishna is clear: willpower and intellect alone won't get you across. Those who surrender to him cross it easily.

visual: The distressed, the curious, the seeker of wealth
And the wise
All are noble; the wise are dearest
scenes.say: Lesson four. Four types of people seek God: the person in distress, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one who has already tasted the Supreme. Krishna calls them all noble. But the wise devotee, whose love asks for nothing, is like his own Self.

visual: Whatever form is worshipped with faith
God makes that faith steady
And fulfils the wish through it
scenes.say: Lesson five. God fulfils every seeker according to their faith. Whatever form a person worships with sincere faith, God makes that faith steady and answers through it. Every sincere prayer reaches the Supreme. Those who ask only for passing things receive passing things; those who seek him reach him.

visual: Of thousands, scarcely one strives
Of those, scarcely one truly knows
Likes and dislikes keep the rest deluded
scenes.say: Lesson six. Rare is the one who truly knows God. Most of us are kept busy, and deluded, by the pairs of opposites: like and dislike, pleasure and pain. Only those whose actions have become pure, and who are free from those pairs, worship him with firm resolve. It takes many lifetimes, and such a soul is very rare.

visual: Knowledge with realisation
After which nothing remains to be known
Knowing God is knowing everything
scenes.say: Lesson seven. Knowing God means knowing everything. Krishna promises Arjuna knowledge together with its realisation, after which nothing remains to be known. True knowledge of the Supreme is not one more fact. It is the one that makes sense of all the others.

scenes.headline: The thread through every jewel
visual: Matter and Spirit both come from God
He is the taste in water, the light in the sun
Surrender carries us across Maya
scenes.say: So, Chapter Seven. Matter and Spirit both come from God, and he runs through everything like the thread through a necklace. He is the taste in water and the light in the sun. His illusion is hard to cross, but surrender carries us over. Next, Arjuna asks about the moment of death.
